risk_register.risk: The order book converts more slowly than either reading here

risk_register.risk: Minority interests absorb more of the value than the book suggests

risk_register.priced_at: computed both ways — at book and proportionally — throughout
risk_register.what_would_change_it: a disclosure of TMG's economic share by project

risk_register.why: four step devaluations since 2016; the cost base and the customer's capacity to pay both move

risk_register.what_would_change_it: a sustained period of currency stability

risk_register.why: a developer that accelerates handovers builds before it collects; the faster reading goes cash-negative from FY2030 and needs funding

risk_register.what_would_change_it: shorter payment plans, or pre-sales collected earlier

risk_register.risk: The Saudi leg is recognised on a different clock
risk_register.why: Banan is percentage-of-completion under EAS 48 while the Egyptian book is point-in-time; it is already 52.5% of segment revenue by 1H2026
risk_register.priced_at: flagged, and excluded from the conversion-rate history

risk_register.risk: Finance cost is not what it appears
risk_register.why: the reported charge implies 44% on interest-bearing debt against a policy rate that peaked near 27.25%; the excess is contract-financing unwind that the statements do not split out
risk_register.priced_at: recorded as a gap; a correction for this line was tested and deliberately not adopted, for the reason given in section 1.6
risk_register.what_would_change_it: the split, or a disclosed average borrowing rate

note: Peer MULTIPLES are not tabulated here. This study holds committed price libraries for the Egyptian names but has not sourced their financial statements, and a peer multiple built on an unsourced denominator is a number wearing a decimal point. The relative lens is therefore built on TMGH's OWN history of multiples, which is sourced end to end, and the peer set is carried as context with its sourcing stated.
